prevention.question: Will this solid keep burning once lit, in ISS-like air?
prevention.source: BASS (PSI-26) crew observations, as-run test matrix

prevention.limits: Labels hand-audited from every crew note. Only 14 of 102 tests failed to keep burning, all at 16-23 % O2 and ~1 atm, and the model learns mostly from material type (Nomex rarely sustained a flame). Its probabilities beat the base rate (lower Brier score). It cannot speak to Moon/Mars atmospheres: no solid was tested above 23 % O2 in the public archive.

detection.question: Which materials make smoke that today's detectors can see, and how much?
detection.source: SAME (PSI-102), SAME-R (PSI-101) instrument logs; SPICE (PSI-107) smoke-point datasheet
detection.limits: Detector 'response' = signal change > max(10x baseline noise, fixed floor); alarm thresholds of flight detectors are not in the data. Particle diameter is a mass/number index (unit density), not a sizing measurement.

suppression.question: Does this atmosphere or agent put the flame out - and does it stay out?
suppression.source: FLEX (PSI-69) + CFI (PSI-39) droplet tests; BASS (PSI-26) nitrogen-flood observations
